summary.headline: Uno Minda Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR6,655 crore and PAT 38% to INR420 crore, with FY27 margin guidance of 11% ±50bps held.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 38% YoY to INR6,655 crore and EBITDA rose 33% to INR733 crore at an 11% margin, with PAT up 38% to INR420 crore; management called it the highest-ever quarterly revenue and profit. Growth was broad-based across switches, lighting, casting (alloy wheels and aluminium die casting), seating and the green mobility vertical, which grew 102%. Management said commodity pass-through is margin dilutive, yet it is holding the full-year margin guidance. Net debt rose to INR2,415 crore from INR2,179 crore at March 2026 while the company announced about INR1,415 crore of new expansion projects in August 2026.

segments.name: Switching systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,609 crore, +37% YoY, about 24% of group revenue; four-wheeler switches (Uno Mindarika) INR617 crore, +30%+. Export switch growth significantly higher.

segments.name: Lighting systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,381 crore, +25% YoY, about 21% of group revenue; led by two-wheeler lighting and EV two-wheeler OEMs; new PV pixel-based headlamp and tail lamp orders.

segments.name: Casting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,441 crore, +57% YoY (includes higher aluminium prices). Four-wheel alloy wheels INR763 crore; two-wheel alloy wheels INR396 crore; aluminium die casting INR282 crore, +65%.

segments.name: Seating systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR476 crore, +34% YoY, about 7% of group revenue; wins with an incumbent Japanese two-wheeler OEM and a bus passenger seat customer.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR649 crore, +102% YoY, about 10% of revenue: EV Systems INR247 crore, alternate fuels INR187 crore, Auto Innovations INR156 crore, EV controllers INR44 crore.

segments.name: Other products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,099 crore, +17% YoY, about 17% of revenue: sensors and ADAS INR261 crore, acoustics INR225 crore, blow moulding INR134 crore, non-EV controllers INR89 crore.

segments.name: Aftermarket and OEM SPD
segments.commentary: Aftermarket INR387 crore (about 6% of revenue); OEM SPD INR323 crore; combined INR709 crore, about 10% of revenue. International business about 9% of revenue; exports about INR218 crore vs INR123 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50bps held despite commodity pass-through being margin dilutive.
Management expects industry growth momentum to continue in H2 FY27 despite a higher base, supported by festive and wedding season and launches.
Alloy wheel capacity to rise over 40% to 9 million wheels per annum, with Kharkhoda and Hosur expansion taking total to about 11.8 million wheels.
Bawal HPDC two-wheel alloy wheel lines 5 and 6 to take capacity from 9 to 9.5 million wheels per annum after commissioning.
Inovance (Khed City) plant expected to be commissioned by end of FY27; Manesar to Farrukhnagar shift to complete in FY27.
Sunroof phase one commissioning around end FY27; additional Bawal sunroof capex of about INR85 crore to be commissioned by Q2 FY28.
Management expects gross contribution and RM-to-sales ratio to improve over time as new business is priced at the new base.

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates and JVs
H1 free cash flow after sustaining capex of INR307 crore

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend in H2 FY27 given expected input cost softening, and how is the Inovance ramp-up progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is holding the 11% ±50bps FY27 margin guidance despite pass-through being margin dilutive; any softening would also be passed back to customers. Inovance (Khed City) is under execution, with commissioning targeted by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the four-wheel alloy wheel step-up, switch growth, and the outlook for RM-to-sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium commodity impact in casting is about INR260-270 crore; wallet share gains came from the Bawal HPDC capacity and casting customer mix. Switch growth reflects exports and mix. RM-to-sales should improve as new business is priced at the new base, alongside operating leverage and gross contribution gains.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost and depreciation trajectory as new capacity comes online?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is near its lowest level at about 11.3% of sales vs 12.5-13.5% earlier; ramp-up may add cost for two years, but manpower cost is not expected to rise sharply once stabilised. Depreciation was up only INR5 crore, helped by WDV method on casting; expect a step-up when the 16 projects are commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental revenue, EBITDA and ROCE from the capex pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial asset turn of about 1.8-2x on new capex, with higher incremental turns on sustaining-model expansions. Target pre-tax ROCE of 18-20% in the third full year of production; blended EBITDA expected within current company profitability range.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on humanoid robotics work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is nothing much to share and was unsure of the source of the question.

capex_capacity: Alloy wheels: installed capacity at 6.3 million wheels per annum after Kharkhoda phase one and Bawal debottlenecking (~20%); target over 40% rise to 9 million wheels per annum, and about 11.8 million with Kharkhoda and Hosur expansion.
Two-wheel alloy wheels: Bawal HPDC facility had 4 of 6 lines running, adding ~1 million units; capacity 8 to 9 million wheels per annum, rising to 9.5 million after the remaining two lines.

Aluminium die casting: Hosur greenfield facility (INR510 crore) approved in August 2026; total August 2026 approvals about INR1,415 crore incl. Kharkhoda two-wheel alloy wheel extension/relocation INR155 crore, Bengaluru moulding expansion INR80 crore, and CSN facility by TGSIN JV ~INR670 crore.
Sunroof: phase one at Bawal due around end FY27; additional ~INR85 crore Bawal capex approved, to be commissioned by Q2 FY28.

Inovance plant at Khed City under execution, expected commissioning by end FY27; Manesar to Farrukhnagar shift on track for FY27 completion. Three new EV charger programs expected to be commissioned in the coming quarter.

H1 FY27 project capex INR500 crore; capex pipeline roughly INR5,200-5,300 crore incl. August approvals; 16 projects under ramp-up or execution. Target pre-tax ROCE 18-20% in third full year; asset turn ~1.8-2x initially on new capex. TG JV commissioned Harohalli, Bengaluru facility, which weighed on its profitability.
demand_pricing: Industry: Q2 FY27 total auto production above 109 lakh units (+~18% YoY); domestic sales +18.2% to 83.9 lakh units; PV production 16.6 lakh (+25%); 2W production 81 lakh (+16.5%); EV 2W registrations +91% to ~5.9 lakh with 11%+ penetration; PV exports -5.2% to 2.29 lakh.

Company revenue +38% YoY to INR6,655 crore; growth attributed to volume plus higher aluminium prices in casting. Aluminium commodity pass-through impact estimated at roughly INR260-270 crore for the quarter.
Switching +37% (2W domestic volumes, favourable mix, export growth 'significantly higher'); 4W switches (Uno Mindarika) +30%+ to INR617 crore.
Casting +57% to INR1,441 crore; 4W alloy wheels INR763 crore; 2W alloy wheels INR396 crore; aluminium die casting +65% to INR282 crore. Wallet-share gains cited in 2W wheels and casting.
Green mobility +102% to INR649 crore; management cites E2W and E3W adoption and higher share with existing and new customers.

Margin: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50bps held; commodity pass-through described as margin dilutive; management expects RM-to-sales and gross contribution to improve as new business is priced at the new base. Employee cost ~11.3% of sales vs 12.5-13.5% earlier.
risks_watch: Commodity-driven margin dilution: aluminium pass-through is margin dilutive, and FY27 margin guidance of 11% ±50bps depends on RM-to-sales improving on new business pricing.

Leverage and capex: net debt rose to INR2,415 crore (from INR2,179 crore at March 2026) with the August 2026 approvals of ~INR1,415 crore and a capex pipeline of ~INR5,200-5,300 crore; project capex INR500 crore in H1.

Execution and ramp-up timing: Inovance (end FY27), Manesar to Farrukhnagar shift (FY27), sunroof phase one (end FY27), Bawal lines 5-6, Kharkhoda and Hosur expansions; 16 projects in ramp-up or execution.
TG JV profitability dragged by fixed cost, depreciation and interest after Harohalli commissioning.
Depreciation and employee cost step-up expected as new plants are commissioned; ROCE at 20.7% includes land bank and CWIP (24.6% ex these).
PV exports down 5.2% and West Asia logistics constraints; management expects H2 FY27 momentum despite higher base.
key_quotes: Despite that, we are holding onto our margin guidance for the full year.

We expect the revenues to be roughly around two in terms of the asset turn, because there are businesses which asset turn is roughly 1.25, 1.3, and there are business where the asset turn is even higher, so up to 2.5 or 3, right?
So our target ROCE is roughly around 18%-20% pre-tax in the third full year of production.
In terms of humanoid, I don't know. There is nothing much I can share about humanoid because I don't know where this honestly came from.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity, with management calling Q2 the highest-ever quarterly revenue and profit. More cautious on margins, acknowledging commodity pass-through is margin dilutive, and evasive on the humanoid question.

rows.label: Employee cost leverage

rows.label: Rising net debt against capex pipeline

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, capacity additions and the record quarter, but cautious on margins given aluminium pass-through dilution; the brief gives no analyst names or detailed Q&A pushback, so analyst tone is inferred from the margin and ramp-up questions.
